title: Aso-ebi palettes that flatter everyone in the group
excerpt: How we help brides and families in Osogbo choose colours that look generous on camera, respect modest silhouettes, and still feel festive.
body:
If you have ever coordinated aso-ebi for a wedding in Nigeria, you know the colour chat is almost as important as the cut. At Lizzy Fusion in Osogbo, we sit with families and look at fabric in daylight first—what sparkles under shop lights can read very different outdoors.

We lean toward rich jewel tones and deep neutrals when the event runs into the evening: emerald, wine, midnight blue, and warm cinnamon read beautifully on a range of skin tones and photograph kindly without harsh contrast. When the brief is brighter, we suggest anchoring with a deeper border or gele so the overall look stays grounded.

Modesty does not mean hiding—it means choosing lines that let you move, greet elders, and dance without tugging. We map blouse lengths, sleeve finishes, and wrapper drape to each person’s comfort, then unify with colour so the group still reads as one story.

If you are planning a celebration this season, bring your date, venue lighting notes, and any family fabrics you must honour. We will sketch options together and follow up on WhatsApp with swatch photos before anyone commits yardage.

— The studio team

title: Reception layers without the bulk
excerpt: Light layering tricks we use for modest reception looks—structure where you want it, air where you need it, and hemlines that stay graceful all evening.
body:
Reception nights in Osun State can swing from warm halls to breezy outdoor photos. Our clients often want coverage they trust, but dread feeling boxed in by too many heavy pieces stacked on top of each other.

We start with breathable base fabrics—cotton voiles, light crepe, or lined georgette—then add structure only where it matters: a defined shoulder, a gentle corseted bodice, or a slim inner belt to carry the weight of the skirt. Outer layers can be detachable capes, sheer evening jackets, or a second wrap that ties at the waist so you can slip it off between dances.

Length is part of comfort. We mark hemlines with the shoes you plan to wear, then walk the studio stairs in them so you know nothing will catch on steps or grass edges. If you love a dramatic train, we add discreet wrist loops or a bustle point so you can gather fabric quickly for the buffet line.

When you book a bespoke reception piece with us, expect honest timelines: embellishment and handwork need room to breathe. We would rather promise a realistic finish date than rush beadwork that should last for memories, not just one night.

Ask us about our current reception calendar on WhatsApp—we are always happy to suggest palettes that pair with what you already own.

— Lizzy Fusion
